chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir from 'Umar ibn Yazid from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever neglects throwing the Jamarat or part of it until the days of Tashreeq have passed, he must throw them the following year. If he does not perform Hajj, his guardian should throw on his behalf. If he has no guardian, he should seek assistance from a Muslim man to throw on his behalf, for the throwing of the Jamarat occurs only during the days of Tashreeq.
And it has been narrated that whoever deliberately leaves throwing the Jamarat, women are not permissible to him, and he must perform Hajj the following year. He narrated that.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.رَمْيَ الْجِمَارِ: Throwing stones at the Jamarat pillars

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for missing the Jamarat throwing during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, clarifying that the days of Tashreeq are the exclusive window for Jamarat throwing, meaning missed throws cannot be made up immediately upon returning to Mecca but must be deferred to the next Hajj season. The text distinguishes between unintentional omission, which requires a proxy (wali or another Muslim) to perform the throws, and deliberate neglect, which carries the heavier penalty of prohibiting marriage until the pilgrim performs Hajj again. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the specific temporal constraints of the ritual and the accountability for intentional omission.
